holidays.name: National Take a Hike Day
holidays.description: Lace up your boots, grab a water bottle, and ditch the screen for a trail. Whether it's a mountain summit or a loop around the neighborhood park, today is your official excuse to go for a walk in nature.
holidays.origin: The American Hiking Society created this observance to encourage people to get outdoors, explore trails, and enjoy the benefits of hiking.
holidays.funFact: Hiking is great for your mood as well as your legs. Studies have linked time spent walking in nature to lower stress and better mental well-being.

holidays.name: National Homemade Bread Day
holidays.description: A day for pulling on an apron, getting flour on your nose, and filling the house with the smell of fresh-baked bread. Sourdough, soda bread, banana bread and cinnamon rolls all count, as long as you made them yourself.
holidays.origin: The observance is tied to a U.S. Senate resolution that proclaimed November 17 as a day to celebrate the tradition of baking bread at home.
holidays.funFact: Bread is among the oldest prepared foods in human history. Archaeologists have found evidence of flatbread baking that dates back thousands of years, well before farming began.

holidays.name: National Butter Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate butter, the creamy ingredient that makes toast, pastries and mashed potatoes better. Spread it on warm bread, melt it over corn, or try making your own.
holidays.origin: National Day Calendar's Registrar proclaimed National Butter Day as an annual observance on November 17.
holidays.funFact: You can make butter at home by shaking heavy cream in a jar until the fat clumps together and separates from the buttermilk. It pairs well with Homemade Bread Day.
